expected: the Jevellan web app "git settings" screen at desktop-light, rendered completely and legibly (one of several screens captured during "Git settings can be saved, reloaded and checked from Projects"; the other steps are judged in their own screenshots)

cosmetic: Thread titles and subtitles in the left sidebar are cut off with ellipses (e.g. 'Context · J11 memory journ…', 'Waiting for you · Browser fixtur…'). This is deliberate truncation, and the key information can still be read.
The 'GitHub token scope' label and dropdown sit outside any card, between the 'GitHub connection' and 'GitHub token' cards. The other settings are inside cards, so this looks inconsistent.
The disabled 'Save Git settings' button has low contrast, but its label can still be read.
The 'Check a project' dropdown shows 'Outside context fixture', which isn't in the visible sidebar project list. This could confuse users, but it is not a rendering problem.
